scenes.title: Five-minute impromptu dream-job speech prep: 'Why am I panicking?' vs 'Okay [Name], you've got this' before stony evaluators
scenes.era: 2014, University of Michigan Emotion & Self-Control Laboratory

layout.description: Bright split-zone psychology laboratory: in the foreground prep desk sits a 5:00 digital countdown clock and two contrasting prep notepad prompts — Card A ('First-Person: Why am I feeling this way?') and Card B ('Named Self-Talk: Why is [Alex] feeling this way?') — separated by a glass partition from a podium facing two stone-faced evaluator mannequins and a pedestal-mounted studio camera.

positions.who: Immersed Speaker A (mannequin in smart-casual shirt)
positions.where: hunched tensely over the 'I / Me' prep card gripping temples as the 5:00 clock ticks down

positions.who: Distanced Speaker B (mannequin in matching smart-casual shirt)
positions.where: sitting upright before the '[Own Name]' coaching card with calm open shoulders, stepping smoothly to the podium
positions.facing: moving from prep desk to podium

positions.where: seated behind the evaluation table scoring speech confidence blind to pronoun condition

props.name: 5:00 countdown speech-prep timer
props.period_detail: crisp tabletop LED clock counting down the 5-minute preparation window

props.name: paired 'I' vs '[Own Name]' silent-reflection cards
props.period_detail: two clean white instruction placards showing the single-pronoun shift

props.name: blind judge rating clipboards ('Confidence / Composure')
props.period_detail: evaluator scorecards showing higher objective speech scores for Named Self-Talk

actions.verb_sequence: stares at 'Why am I nervous?' card -> shoulders tighten and speech notes tremble
reads 'Why is [Alex] nervous?' card -> exhales, squares shoulders, and delivers a clear, poised speech at the podium while blind judges mark high confidence scores

reactions.reaction: nod and mark noticeably higher composure bars for Speaker B
steps down calm without post-speech cringing

scenes.wardrobe: 2014 university smart-casual shirts, blazers for evaluators.
scenes.recognition_hook: Five minutes to prepare a surprise dream-job speech in front of stone-faced judges — and changing 'I' to your own first name visibly transforms how calm you sound.

key_visual.description: a psychology speech-test room with a 5-minute countdown clock and 'I' versus '[Own Name]' reflection cards in front of a podium and two clipboard evaluators

scenes.title: 2017 Sub-Second EEG Calming Without Extra Effort

positions.where: sitting calmly as the Late Positive Potential emotional wave drops smoothly on '[Name]' trials

reactions.reaction: notes zero spike in effortful frontal load

positions.where: writing one brief coaching takeaway by name and closing the notebook peacefully
